prediction.text:
Disney said Experiences segment operating income rose $723 million, from $9,272 million to $9,995 million, in fiscal 2025. It attributed the increase to growth at domestic parks and experiences and, to a lesser extent, consumer products and international parks and experiences. Disney also described higher costs that partly offset the growth. It said depreciation and amortization rose $244 million, from $2,579 million to $2,823 million.
Disney reported that Experiences segment operating income increased $723 million, from $9,272 million to $9,995 million. It attributed the increase to growth at domestic parks and experiences and, to a lesser extent, consumer products and international parks and experiences.
On the revenue side, Disney said theme park admissions revenue increased 4% from higher average per capita ticket revenue. It said passenger cruise days increased because of the launch of the Disney Treasure in the first quarter of the year.
Higher costs partly offset the growth. Disney said the increase in operating labor was due to inflation, new guest offerings and higher volumes. It said higher infrastructure costs were primarily attributable to higher technology spending, new guest offerings and an increase in operations support costs, partially offset by cost management initiatives.
Disney said the increase in other operating expenses was primarily attributable to new guest offerings, higher volumes and increased operations support costs, partially offset by cost management initiatives. It said depreciation and amortization increased $244 million, from $2,579 million to $2,823 million, primarily due to higher depreciation at domestic parks and experiences driven by an increase at Disney Cruise Line.
